title: Boss: refunds went missing
summary: Find the routing keys nothing matches, route a traffic sample through the real bindings, end a poison loop with a delivery limit and track publisher confirms.

steps.title: INC-5530: refunds never reach the refunds service
body: > Since release 2.14 of orders-api (yesterday 17:00), no refund has reached refunds-worker. orders-api logs
> every publish as successful. Separately, billing-consumer has been at 100 % CPU since 06:00: the same
> message is redelivered thousands of times per minute and everything behind it waits.
orders-api  INF Published refund.issued.eu MessageId=rf-2291      (2.14 renamed the key)
billing     WRN MessageId=ord-7781 Redelivered=True JsonException: '0x00' is invalid after a value
1. List the routing keys from yesterday's traffic sample that **no** binding on `orders` matches.
2. Route the whole sample through the bindings as `rabbitmqctl list_bindings` prints them, catching what does
not route in an alternate-exchange queue, so nothing is lost while the key is fixed.
3. Show that a delivery limit ends the poison loop and lets the other messages through.
4. Make orders-api track publisher confirms, so a nack or a return is never logged as success again.

steps.title: Which keys go nowhere?
prompt: Write `List<string> Unmatched(string[] bindingKeys, string[] routingKeys)`: the routing keys that **no**
binding key matches with topic rules (`*` exactly one word, `#` zero or more), **each once**, in the order they
first appear. Paste in your `TopicMatches` from the cold rebuild (the editor does not have it) and call it.
```text
Unmatched(["order.*.created", "order.#", "refund.*.issued"],
["order.eu.created", "refund.issued.eu", "refund.eu.issued", "refund.issued.eu"])
→ ["refund.issued.eu"]
solution: static bool Match(string[] p, int i, string[] k, int j)
return Match(p, i + 1, k, j) || (j < k.Length && Match(p, i, k, j + 1));
return j < k.Length && (p[i] == "*" || p[i] == k[j]) && Match(p, i + 1, k, j + 1);
hints: Reuse your topic matcher; a key is unmatched when `!bindingKeys.Any(b => TopicMatches(b, k))`.
template: Dojo.Eq("the renamed refund key", new List<string> { "refund.issued.eu" }, Unmatched(new[] { "order.*.created", "order.#", "refund.*.issued" }, new[] { "order.eu.created", "refund.issued.eu", "refund.eu.issued", "refund.issued.eu" }));
Dojo.Eq("everything routes", new List<string>(), Unmatched(new[] { "#" }, new[] { "a", "b.c" }));
Dojo.Eq("no bindings: every key, once, in order", new List<string> { "b", "a" }, Unmatched(new string[0], new[] { "b", "a", "b" }));

Dojo.Eq("star needs exactly one word", new List<string> { "refund.issued", "refund.eu.b2b.issued" }, Unmatched(new[] { "refund.*.issued" }, new[] { "refund.issued", "refund.eu.issued", "refund.eu.b2b.issued" }));

steps.title: Route the sample through the real bindings
prompt: Write
`Dictionary<string, List<string>> RouteSample(string listBindingsOutput, string exchange, string[] routingKeys, string alternateQueue)`.
`listBindingsOutput` is what `rabbitmqctl list_bindings source_name destination_name routing_key` prints:
one row per line, columns separated by **tabs**; lines may end in `\n` or `\r\n`. Skip any line that does
not have exactly 3 columns and the header row (`source_name`). Use only rows whose source is `exchange`
(default-exchange rows have an empty source); they are topic bindings. Include your `TopicMatches` again.
For each routing key, in order: every matching destination queue (each once per message) gets the key appended
to its list. A key that matches nothing is appended to `alternateQueue` instead. Only queues that received
something appear in the result.

steps.title: End the poison loop
prompt: A classic queue puts a requeued message back at its original place, the **front**, so a poison message comes
straight back and blocks everything behind it. A delivery limit ends the loop.
Write `List<string> Drain(string[] messages, Func<string, bool> handler, int deliveryLimit)` for one consumer:
- take the message at the front, count this delivery (`n` = 1, 2, ... per message) and call `handler(message)`;
- `true` → log `"{message} #{n} ack"`;
- `false` and the message has now failed **more than `deliveryLimit` times** → log `"{message} #{n} dead-letter"`
and drop it from the queue;
- otherwise log `"{message} #{n} requeue"` and put it back at the **front**;
- stop when the queue is empty and return the log.
With `deliveryLimit = 2`, a message that always fails is delivered 3 times.
starter: List<string> Drain(string[] messages, Func<string, bool> handler, int deliveryLimit)
solution: List<string> Drain(string[] messages, Func<string, bool> handler, int deliveryLimit)
hints: A `LinkedList<string>` makes "back to the front" cheap: `AddFirst`.
Count deliveries per message in a dictionary; the failure that pushes the count above the limit dead-letters.
template: Dojo.Eq("the poison message is cut off, the rest flows", new List<string> { "m1 #1 ack", "poison #1 requeue", "poison #2 requeue", "poison #3 dead-letter", "m3 #1 ack" }, Drain(new[] { "m1", "poison", "m3" }, m => m != "poison", 2));

Dojo.Eq("a transient failure recovers on the next delivery", new List<string> { "flaky #1 requeue", "flaky #2 ack", "m2 #1 ack" }, Drain(new[] { "flaky", "m2" }, m => { if (dojoFails.GetValueOrDefault(m) > 0) { dojoFails[m]--; return false; } return true; }, 5));
Dojo.Eq("limit 0: dead-letter on the first failure", new List<string> { "bad #1 dead-letter", "ok #1 ack" }, Drain(new[] { "bad", "ok" }, m => m == "ok", 0));
Dojo.Eq("nothing to drain", new List<string>(), Drain(new string[0], _ => true, 3));

steps.title: Track publisher confirms
prompt: Under RabbitMQ.Client 7's confirmation tracking is a simple protocol. Write it yourself, so you know what a
`PublishException` means. Write a class `ConfirmTracker`:
- `long Publish(string messageId)`: returns the next sequence number (`1`, `2`, ...); the message is outstanding.
- `void Ack(long seq, bool multiple)`: confirms that outstanding message, or with `multiple` every outstanding
message with a sequence number up to `seq`.
- `void Nack(long seq, bool multiple)`: the same selection, but those messages must be republished: add their
ids to `ToRepublish`.
- `void Return(string messageId)`: a `basic.return` arrived (unroutable with `mandatory`); add the id to
`Unroutable`. The broker still acks it afterwards.
- Sequence numbers that are not outstanding are ignored.
- `List<string> Outstanding` (ids in sequence order), `List<string> ToRepublish`, `List<string> Unroutable`.
starter: public void Ack(long seq, bool multiple) { }
public void Nack(long seq, bool multiple) { }
solution: public void Ack(long seq, bool multiple) => Settle(seq, multiple);
public void Nack(long seq, bool multiple) => ToRepublish.AddRange(Settle(seq, multiple));
var keys = outstanding.Keys.Where(k => multiple ? k <= seq : k == seq).ToList();
hints: A `SortedDictionary<long, string>` keeps outstanding messages in sequence order.
Ack and nack share one helper that removes the selected sequence numbers and returns their ids.
template: Dojo.Eq("multiple ack confirms 1 and 2", new List<string> { "o3", "o4", "o5" }, dojoT.Outstanding);
Dojo.Eq("single ack confirms only 4", new List<string> { "o3", "o5" }, dojoT.Outstanding);
Dojo.Eq("the returned message is flagged", new List<string> { "o4" }, dojoT.Unroutable);
Dojo.Eq("multiple nack: republish 3 and 5", new List<string> { "o3", "o5" }, dojoT.ToRepublish);
Dojo.Eq("unknown sequence numbers are ignored", 0, dojoT.Outstanding.Count);
